correctness.rationale: The quadratic regression risk follows from stochastic Fubini and Itô isometry. Compactness of the sorted site simplex gives attainment. After merging positive repeated sites the Brownian precision matrix plus the inverse noise matrix is a strictly diagonally dominant M-matrix; the computed K^{-1}k is strictly positive, giving positive weights at every positive site. Replacing an unused zero site is a strict improvement by a nonzero residual partial covariance. At an interior knot of multiplicity m, symmetric splitting changes the loss at first order by -2(m-1)v² times the displacement; at 1, moving one of m copies left changes it by -(2m-1)v² times the displacement. Subtracting the interior normal equations forces consecutive weights equal because the multiplier is η+(v_i+v_{i+1})/8>0. The smaller quadratic root is the only feasible one; the larger lies above 2/(2n-1). The projection identity then gives the claimed risk. Uniqueness is of the sorted design, or up to permutation of sensor labels. The companion verify.py was inspected, not executed; it uses rational perturbations for n≤4 and does not certify the continuous search. The proof, not the finite checks, establishes global optimality.

evidence: The joint design searches all deterministic times and all positive precisions summing to P, including every fixed-variance design at P=n/η. The joint optimum is unique up to simultaneous relabeling and is strictly interior without replication.
